extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants and their legal/accounting/compliance advisors preparing SEC filings (Regulation S-K) on climate-related matters
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and filing SEC disclosures required by the final climate-related rules (Regulation S-K Items such as 1500–1508), including materiality assessments, transition plans, expenditures disclosure, and related structured-data filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality standard for climate disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is material if there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable investor would consider the information important in deciding how to vote or make an investment decision; an omitted fact is material if its disclosure would have significantly altered the total mix of information available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 17 CFR 230.405 and 17 CFR 240.12b-2; Basic Inc. v. Levinson, 485 U.S. 224 (1988); TSC Industries v. Northway, 426 U.S. 438 (1977). Litwin v. Blackstone (quantitative and qualitative factors considered integratively). Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 99 warns registrants/auditors not to substitute a percentage threshold for materiality. See also Concept Release (Release No. 33-10064).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably likely standard (application to climate risks)
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing whether climate-related risks are material or reasonably likely to occur, management must make a thoughtful and objective evaluation based on materiality; the 'reasonably likely' standard does not require registrants to affirm the non-existence or non-occurrence of a material future event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants can look to the 2020 MD&A Adopting Release for application of the 'reasonably likely' standard: it requires an integrative, objective judgment where fruition of future events is unknown (2020 MD&A Adopting Release, 86 FR at 2093).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation not to make materially misleading statements or omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants have a fundamental obligation not to make materially misleading statements or omissions in their disclosures and may need to provide additional information necessary to keep disclosures from being misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 17 CFR 230.408 and 17 CFR 240.12b-20. If additional information is needed to avoid misleading investors, registrants must include it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for disclosing transition risk in value chains
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant need only disclose the transition risk of a party in its value chain when such transition risk has materially impacted or is reasonably likely to materially impact the registrant itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits value-chain disclosure to information that is material to the registrant rather than all upstream/downstream risks; see 17 CFR 229.1500 definition of transition risk for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'transition risk'
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition risk means actual or potential negative impacts on a registrant's business, results of operations, or financial condition attributable to regulatory, technological, and market changes to address mitigation of, or adaptation to, climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include increased costs from changes in law or policy, reduced market demand for carbon‑intensive products (price/profit declines), devaluation/abandonment of assets, legal liability and litigation defense costs, competitive pressures from new technologies, and reputational impacts that change market/consumer/registrant behavior (see 17 CFR 229.1500).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of liability and reputational impacts in Item 1502(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 1502(a)(2) omits a specific reference to liability and reputational factors to align with Item 1500's definition that refers to regulatory, technological, and market changes; however, if a registrant has incurred or is reasonably likely to incur a material negative impact to reputation or liability, it must describe that impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change intended to avoid undue emphasis on liability/reputation over other transition impacts; registrants must include any material transition-related impacts in Item 1502(a)(2) disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'outlook' in Item 1502(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: As used in the final rules, 'outlook' means 'the prospect for the future' and is not intended to require or suggest disclosure of earnings guidance or forecasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites general dictionary definition (Merriam‑Webster) and clarifies scope to avoid implying an obligation to provide financial guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material contracts disclosure requirement (Item 1502(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are required to include material contracts in Commission filings under existing rules; Item 1502(b)(3) references that obligation in the climate-disclosure context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 17 CFR 229.601(b)(10) and the cross-reference from Item 1502(b)(3). Ensure material climate-related contracts are filed where required by existing material contracts rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material expenditures disclosure for mitigation/adaptation activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose material expenditures and material impacts on financial estimates and assumptions that directly result from mitigation or adaptation activities (e.g., transition activities expenditures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure may overlap across Items 1502(d)(2), 1502(e) (transition plans), and 1504(c)(2) (targets/goals). To avoid redundancy, registrants should disclose material expenditures under the Item where most appropriate and cross‑reference to that disclosure when responding to other Items. Examples: costs to electrify fleets, renewable energy purchases, carbon offset purchases (see commenters/Appendix A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured data requirement (Item 1508) for expenditures and related disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 1508's structured-data requirements are intended to facilitate investors' ability to find and analyze material expenditures disclosure regardless of whether provided in tabular or narrative form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should provide the required expenditures information in the structured format specified by Item 1508 to improve investor analysis and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in timing for material expenditures disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission provides a one-year phase-in for the material expenditures disclosure requirements adopted in connection with a transition plan or a target and goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section II.O. The one-year phase-in is intended to ease compliance burdens as registrants begin disclosing under the final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation between Regulation S-X amendments and Regulation S-K expenditure disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendments to Regulation S-X do not require disclosure of expenditures to mitigate risks of severe weather events; Regulation S-K Item 1502 will therefore produce some physical‑risk expenditure information not otherwise required by Reg S‑X. Conversely, Reg S‑X amendments require disclosure of expenditures related to carbon offsets and RECs in notes to the financial statements when used as a material component to achieve disclosed climate-related targets/goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must reconcile overlapping requirements: some expenditure disclosures will appear in financial-statement notes (Reg S‑X) and some under Reg S‑K; cross‑referencing rules (see below) govern how to avoid redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-referencing rules between Regulation S-K and financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may cross-reference to information in their financial statements to satisfy Regulation S‑K disclosure obligations, but they are not permitted to cross-reference from Regulation S‑K disclosures to Regulation S‑K disclosures in their financial statements unless specifically permitted by Commission rules or by applicable U.S. GAAP or IFRS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 17 CFR 230.411 and 17 CFR 240.12b-23. Use cross-references carefully to comply with these limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan disclosure content and updates (Item 1502(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition plan disclosure is required as part of a registrant's discussion of climate-related risks and their impact on strategy. Registrants should disclose plan objectives (short-, medium-, long-term), the levers to achieve them, and metrics used to track progress; updates are required while the plan is used to manage a material transition risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rules include transition plan disclosure consistent with TCFD recommendations. Registrants need not update disclosure if the transition plan is no longer used to manage a material transition risk. See 17 CFR 229.1502(e) and related discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding redundant or immaterial disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures should be eliminated if immaterial or redundant so as not to obscure relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle echoes TCFD recommendations and commenter input (e.g., Chamber). Registrants should focus on material, non-redundant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario analysis as a tool for climate disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenario analysis is a process for identifying and assessing a potential range of outcomes of future events under conditions of uncertainty and is used to inform registrants' assessments of climate-related risks and transition plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See TCFD definition and Proposing Release discussion; scenario analysis can support disclosures about resilience, strategy, and transition planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Significant contributing factor" attribution principle (financial statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'significant contributing factor' attribution principle applies to certain disclosures required by the final rules in the financial statements but does not pertain to the expenditure disclosure obligations in Regulation S‑K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See discussion in section II.K.3.c; treat attribution standards differently depending on whether disclosure is in financial statements (Reg S‑X) or Regulation S‑K narrative/tabular disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-horizon definitions are fact-specific (commenter input)
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevant time periods for short-term and long-term impacts are fact- and registrant-specific; some commenters suggested short-term be 18–24 months and long-term be anything over 24 months, but the Commission treats time horizons as dependent on particular facts and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should define and apply horizons consistent with their specific business and materiality judgments rather than fixed bright-line timeframes, while noting commenter suggestions where appropriate.
